newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says economy not overheating.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says economy not overheating.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Wednesday doused fears the economy was overheating following robust growth in the first nine months of the year.
Ramos told his weekly news conference he did not expect inflation to rise in December despite prospects of another round of local oil price hikes.

"It's not overheating. Do (you) consider a growth rate in real terms as overheating?", Ramos asked. "The economies in East Asia and the Asia-Pacific that are overheating were going at 15 percent a year and maybe more."
Ramos said there was plenty of room in the Philippines for more investments.

Last week's announcement that Philippine gross national product grew by 7.1 percent in the first nine months of the year from the year-ago 5.3 percent had prompted businessmen to watch out for dangers signs of a "bubble bursting."

Ramos, who has won praise for steering the country's growth by introducing reforms at the start of his tenure in 1992, said he has set a Philippine average target growth rate of between six and eight percent starting 1997 to 2002.
"Now that we are approaching the double-digit period, all of a sudden some people are getting scared," he said.
"Just relax. don't be tense, otherwise you might collapse," Ramos added.
